summary: The article argues that nations must invest heavily in cybersecurity research and development to keep pace with evolving cyber threats, with implications for national security strategy after September 1, 2023. It covers public-private collaboration, quantum-resistant cryptography, secure IoT frameworks, AI-driven threat prevention, and workforce education, citing named experts and dated initiatives. It concludes that the race against cyber threats is unending and requires sustained commitment.
one_line: Article arguing nations must invest in cybersecurity R&D across cryptography, IoT, AI threat prevention, collaboration and workforce training to stay ahead of threats.
key_facts: Dr. Linda Sterling and cyber analyst James McKenzie were on an expert panel at the International Cybersecurity Forum last October that stressed proactive and preemptive cyber defense.
Dr. Linda Sterling warned that without continuous R&D, defensive measures will become obsolete, and advocated a "sustained and incentivized R&D ecosystem."
The Cybersecurity Innovation Hub was launched on November 15, 2023, bringing together tech companies, academic institutions, and government agencies to co-develop cybersecurity solutions.
Ian Richards, director of the Cybersecurity Innovation Hub, said the Hub provides a collaborative R&D platform and helps convert research into deployable cyber defense tools.
Cryptographer Alice Bennett presented a new post-quantum encryption algorithm at the Quantum Computing Showcase on December 3, 2023.
Quantum computing threatens current encryption methods, so substantial R&D resources go toward quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms.
SecureTech announced on September 20, 2023 a breakthrough in lightweight encryption for small IoT devices.
SecureTech CTO Michael Peterson said the approach ensures even the most constrained devices have robust protection.
Sophia Chan, lead AI strategist at CyberAI Labs, spoke at the annual Cybersecurity R&D Symposium on January 29, 2024 about training AI systems to think like hackers.
AI and machine learning systems can analyze patterns, detect anomalies, and counteract breaches in real time.
The National Cyber Security Education Initiative (NCSEI) was expanded on February 12, 2024 and integrates hands-on experience with cutting-edge R&D projects.
NCSEI director Edward Grant said immersing students and professionals in real-world R&D prepares them to lead future developments.
